external_mappings.notes: Senses separated: H5869 denotes both anatomical eye (most frequent) and water spring (e.g. Gen 16:7). Occurrence context decides which sense applies.

Polysemous lemma H5869 ("eye" vs "spring"); hydrology sense applies specifically in water-source passages (e.g. Gen 16:7, Gen 24:13). Marked candidate at lemma level pending occurrence disambiguation.
Hebrew be'er: excavated or natural shaft yielding groundwater (e.g. Gen 16:14, Gen 21:19).
Primary Hebrew word for physical water.
Greek pege: natural spring or fountain (e.g. John 4:6, Jas 3:11).
Greek phrear: deep excavated well/shaft (e.g. John 4:11-12).
Primary Greek word for physical water.
Primary Greek anatomical word for eye.
Hebrew ner: ancient oil-fed lamp (distinct from multi-branched lampstand H4501 menorah).
Hebrew menorah: sanctuary lampstand holding lamps (Exod 25:31-37, Zech 4:2).
Hebrew lappid: hand-carried flaming torch.
Hebrew shemen: pressed olive oil used for anointing and sanctuary lamps (Exod 27:20, Zech 4:12).
Greek lychnos: portable oil lamp (e.g. Matt 5:15, Luke 11:34).
Greek lychnia: lampstand (domestic or sanctuary; Rev 1:20 explicitly equates seven lampstands with seven churches).
Greek lampas: oil-fed torch or lamp (Matt 25:1-8, Rev 4:5); keeps torch vs oil lamp distinction explicit.
Greek phos has both physical illumination and theological/metaphorical senses; modern optical concept applies only to physical referents.
ruach spans spirit, wind, and breath. Do NOT project physical wind/breath onto occurrences referring to the Spirit of God without contextual evidence.
Breath sense of ruach, overlapping with H5397 neshamah.
Hebrew neshamah: life-breath / respiration (Gen 2:7).
Greek pneuma spans Spirit/spirit, wind (John 3:8), and breath; physical mapping is strictly candidate.
Hebrew shani: crimson/scarlet dyed wool/thread.
Greek kokkinos: scarlet/crimson (e.g. Heb 9:19, Rev 17:3).
Botanical identification of biblical ezov is most commonly Origanum syriacum (Syrian oregano) rather than European Hyssopus officinalis.
Greek hyssopos (Heb 9:19, John 19:29).
Hebrew erez: Lebanon cedar / aromatic timber.
Hebrew rimmon: pomegranate fruit or carved sanctuary ornament.
Hebrew zahav: gold.
Hebrew nechoshet covers both unalloyed copper and copper-tin bronze.
Hebrew dam: biological blood (not to be conflated with H0120 adam).
Greek haima: biological blood.
Hebrew zera spans agricultural seed and genealogical offspring; physical concept applies to botanical sense.
Greek sporos: sown seed.
Greek sperma: botanical seed and metaphorical offspring.
Hebrew lechem: bread / baked food.
Greek artos: baked bread / loaf.
Hebrew eben: mineral stone or cut building stone.
Greek lithos: stone.
Hebrew esh: physical fire / combustion.
Hebrew ashan: smoke produced by fire/combustion.
Hebrew keseph denotes both silver metal and silver money/shekels.
Hebrew barzel: metallic iron.
Hebrew melach: mineral/table salt (used in covenantal offerings and Salt Sea names).
Greek halas: salt (Matt 5:13, Mark 9:50, Col 4:6).
Hebrew chittah: wheat grain (and standing wheat crop).
Greek sitos: wheat or cereal grain (Matt 13:25, John 12:24).
Hebrew seorah: barley grain.
Greek krithinos: adjective denoting barley-grain composition (John 6:9, 6:13).
Hebrew gephen: grapevine (Vitis).
Greek ampelos: grapevine (John 15:1-5).
Hebrew teenah denotes both fig tree and fig fruit.
Greek suke: fig tree (Matt 21:19, Luke 13:6).
Hebrew shemesh: sun.
Greek helios: sun.
Hebrew tsemer: sheep wool fiber.
Greek erion: wool (Heb 9:19, Rev 1:14).
Hebrew chamets covers fermenting leaven and leavened food.
Hebrew seor: fermenting leaven / sourdough starter.
Greek zume: physical leaven (Matt 13:33) and metaphorical teaching/influence (Matt 16:6).
Hebrew matstsah: unleavened bread.
Greek azumos: unleavened bread or Festival of Unleavened Bread.
Hebrew chomer: potter clay or mud mortar.
Greek pelos: potter clay or wet clay/mud (John 9:6, Rom 9:21).
Polysemous lemma H7198 qeshet: archery bow (most frequent) vs rainbow (Gen 9:13).
Polysemous lemma H7198 qeshet: rainbow sense in Gen 9:13-16 and Ezek 1:28.
